hook.text: Digital cameras started terrible. Blurry, expensive, limited. Kodak ignored them.

buildup.text: Clayton Christensen showed that disruption starts at the bottom of a market with inferior products that are cheaper.

discovery.text: Christensen published The Innovator's Dilemma in 1997.

twist.text: The disruptor improves rapidly. By the time the incumbent notices, the new technology has overtaken them.

climax.text: Watch what your worst customers prefer. Your best customers will dismiss it. But the cheap.

punchline.text: Disruption starts where leaders least expect it.

quiz.question: Where does disruptive innovation typically start?
options: At the premium end of the market
At the bottom with inferior products
